key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical neural network can learn nonlocal features of quantum phases and reliably recognize topological ground states on superconducting hardware.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path for quantum-phase classification tasks where classical sample complexity becomes expensive, using near-term quantum processors in the training loop.
method: Hardware-efficient parameterized quantum circuit + feedforward neural network
Joint end-to-end training with superconducting quantum hardware
Classify surface code lattice states against featureless product-state ensembles
evidence_signal: The classifier achieved over 85% accuracy in single-shot measurements and above 99% when predictions were averaged over ten measurements.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on small surface-code lattices and depends on repeated measurements, so scaling and hardware noise robustness remain key concerns.
paper_title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Recognizing Quantum Phases
